title: Build an executive assistant agent
use_case: Build an executive assistant agent that helps me manage email, calendar, meetings, follow-ups and briefings.
outcome: A personal assistant agent that triages your inbox, drafts replies in your style, proposes meeting times, prepares briefing notes before meetings, tracks follow-ups and actions, and remembers your preferences. It acts only with your approval, under access controls you set. You will also know when a ready-made assistant in your existing tools is the better choice.
assumptions: You are willing to learn or refresh basic Python, or will use the low-code Microsoft route in capability 5.
Your email, calendar and documents live in Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.
The agent drafts and proposes; you approve anything sent, accepted or deleted, at least until it has proved reliable.

capabilities.name: Decide what to delegate
capabilities.why: An assistant is only useful if it is clear which tasks it may do alone, which it drafts for approval, and which stay with you.

steps.why: Free, short framework for delegating to AI and checking its work; the basis of the assistant's job description.
Highly rated non-technical primer on what generative AI can and cannot do reliably.

capabilities.name: Python foundations
capabilities.why: Most agent frameworks and email or calendar APIs are used from Python.

steps.why: Skip if you already write Python, or if you take the low-code route in capability 5.

capabilities.name: Prompting, structured output and tool use
capabilities.why: Triage, drafting in your voice and extracting actions from email all depend on reliable prompts and structured output; scheduling needs tool calls.

steps.why: Hands-on course in prompt engineering, prompt evaluation and tool use with an LLM API.
Highly rated, deeper prompt-engineering practice for drafting and summarising.

capabilities.name: Agent design and memory
capabilities.why: The assistant must plan multi-step tasks and remember your preferences, key contacts, past decisions and standing rules.

steps.why: Core agent design patterns: reflection, tool use, planning and multi-agent work.
Builds an email assistant with semantic, episodic and procedural memory: very close to this use case.
Deeper, project-based agent practice with an assessed certificate.

capabilities.name: Connect to email, calendar and documents
capabilities.why: The assistant needs controlled access to your mailbox, calendar, contacts and files.

steps.why: One-hour introduction to MCP, the standard way to connect an assistant to tools and data.
Build and connect MCP servers, so you can use or adapt existing email and calendar connectors.
Low-code route if you use Microsoft 365: build agents that already sit next to Outlook, Teams and SharePoint.

capabilities.gap: No verified course yet teaches the Gmail and Google Calendar APIs, the Microsoft Graph API or OAuth permission scopes for a personal assistant. Use the official API documentation for now.

capabilities.name: Search your own knowledge
capabilities.why: Meeting briefings need context from past email threads, notes, documents and decisions, retrieved accurately with sources.

steps.why: Free, project-based course in building and evaluating retrieval (RAG) systems.

capabilities.name: Secure it against untrusted content
capabilities.why: Every incoming email is untrusted input. A malicious message can try to make the assistant leak data or take actions (prompt injection), so access and actions must be tightly limited.

steps.why: Short, hands-on introduction to prompt injection and red-teaming LLM applications.
In-depth GenAI application security course with a GIAC exam option. Expensive; take it if the assistant will handle other people's data.

capabilities.gap: No verified course yet focuses on securing tool-using agents that read email (least-privilege access, approval gates, data-loss controls).

capabilities.name: Privacy, oversight and accountability
capabilities.why: The assistant processes personal data of colleagues and contacts, so GDPR, retention and human oversight apply.

steps.why: Short, highly rated overview of AI governance and oversight principles to apply to your assistant.

capabilities.gap: No verified course yet covers GDPR obligations specifically for personal AI assistants.

capabilities.name: Test it and run it daily
capabilities.why: Wrong triage or a bad draft costs trust quickly. The assistant needs test cases, then a reliable daily schedule with logs.

steps.why: In-depth course on evaluating LLM products and analysing errors. Expensive; worth it if others will use the assistant.

capabilities.gap: No verified course in the database yet teaches scheduling and hosting a small personal agent (cron jobs, serverless functions, secrets handling).

milestones.name: Write the assistant's job description
milestones.deliverable: One-page spec: which tasks it does alone, drafts for approval, or never touches; the tone it writes in; who it may contact; what it may read.

milestones.name: Inbox triage on exported mail
milestones.deliverable: A script that sorts a sample of your exported email into act, delegate, read later and ignore, extracts actions and deadlines, and drafts replies in your style. No live access yet.

milestones.name: Memory of you
milestones.deliverable: Stored preferences, key contacts and standing rules that the assistant uses and updates, for example meeting-time preferences and who gets priority.

milestones.name: Read-only live connection
milestones.deliverable: The assistant reads your mailbox and calendar with the narrowest permissions available, cannot send or delete, and passes your own prompt-injection tests.

milestones.name: Daily briefing
milestones.deliverable: Each morning: today's meetings with a briefing note per meeting (who, history, open items, sources), urgent emails, and overdue follow-ups.

milestones.name: Supervised actions and pilot
milestones.deliverable: Drafts and calendar proposals that you approve with one click, an audit log, a privacy note, accuracy measured over two weeks, and a buy-versus-build comparison with the assistants built into Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.

research_queue: Courses on the Gmail, Google Calendar and Microsoft Graph APIs, and OAuth scopes for assistants.
Training on securing tool-using agents against prompt injection (least privilege, approval gates).
GDPR and data-protection training for AI assistants, preferably from Irish or EU bodies.
Google Workspace (Gemini) and Microsoft 365 Copilot agent-building training, to compare buy with build.
Deploying and scheduling small agents with course-specific evidence.
notes: The AI project manager pack shares several capabilities (LLM API, agents, MCP, retrieval). Training taken for one counts for the other.
Your email and calendar provider probably already offers a built-in assistant. Compare it with your milestone 1 spec before building everything yourself.
Keep the assistant read-only and draft-only until testing shows it is reliable and resistant to prompt injection.
